findings.title: Async legacy writes use the request context, which is cancelled when the handler returns
findings.body: All four async goroutines (Create line 51, Delete line 110, Update line 135, DeleteCollection line 163) derive their context via `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` from the handler's request `ctx`. In the Kubernetes apiserver (net/http) the request context is cancelled as soon as the handler returns, which happens immediately after these goroutines are spawned. The legacy call therefore usually receives an already-cancelled context and aborts before writing. The whole point of mode 3 (best-effort async replication to legacy as a safety net) will silently not happen. Detach first, e.g. `context.WithTimeoutCause(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), ...)`, so the goroutine is not tied to the request lifetime.

findings.title: Unified-storage errors are recorded on the legacy metric (and storage errors not counted)
findings.body: In Create the error branch after `d.Storage.Create` records `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` using `startStorage`; it should record a storage-failure metric (`recordStorageDuration(true, ...)`). The same mistake exists in Update at line 129. As a result a failed unified-storage write is reported as a legacy-write failure, the unified-storage error rate is under-reported, and the legacy error rate is inflated, making the metrics misleading for exactly the failure everyone cares about.

findings.title: Delete success path passes the object name as the `kind` label
findings.body: On the success path of Delete, `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the object `name` where the metric expects the resource `kind` (every other call site passes `options.Kind`). This mislabels the metric and, worse, makes the `kind` label take on every individual object name, causing unbounded label cardinality in the Prometheus metric. Use `options.Kind`.

findings.title: Legacy DeleteCollection result recorded with the storage metric
findings.body: Inside the DeleteCollection goroutine the legacy call's outcome is recorded via `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)`. It should be `d.recordLegacyDuration(...)`, consistent with the other legacy branches. As written, legacy delete-collection failures/successes are attributed to the unified-storage metric and the legacy metric never sees them.

findings.title: Delete stores the unfielded logger in the context
findings.body: Delete builds `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)` but then does `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of `klog.NewContext(ctx, log)`. The context passed to `d.Storage.Delete` and to the async legacy goroutine therefore lacks the name/kind/method fields, so log lines from these operations cannot be correlated as intended. Should use `log`.

findings.title: Async legacy write failures are no longer logged
findings.body: The previous synchronous implementation logged errors from the legacy write (`unwrap...Error(err, "unable to create object in legacy storage")`, etc.). The new goroutines (Create line 55, Delete line 112, Update line 139, DeleteCollection line 165) only increment a metric and never log `errObjectSt`/`err`. Combined with the context-cancellation issue above, legacy writes can fail completely invisibly; operators have no log line to diagnose drift between unified and legacy storage. Log the error (with kind/name) inside the goroutine.

findings.title: Tests do not verify or synchronize the async legacy writes
findings.body: The new unit tests set up legacy mock expectations but never assert them (no `m.AssertExpectations` on the legacy calls) and provide no synchronization (channel / `require.Eventually`) to wait for the spawned goroutines. Because the legacy write happens in a goroutine that may run after the subtest returns, the tests pass even if the legacy write never occurs, so the central new behavior of mode 3 (async dual write) is effectively untested. Add a wait/assertion that each legacy Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection is actually invoked with the expected object.

findings.title: Mode 3 integration runs assume immediate legacy consistency but legacy writes are async
findings.body: The newly added mode 3 subtests (file at line 132, unified storage at line 191) reuse `doPlaylistTests`, which after a k8s create/update immediately asserts the same object is visible through the legacy API (the `/api/playlists` list compare and `getFromBothAPIs` legacy GET). In mode 3 the write to the legacy/SQL store happens asynchronously in a goroutine, so those assertions can observe stale data and fail intermittently. Either wait for eventual consistency (e.g. poll the legacy API) for mode 3, or don't run the synchronous legacy-consistency assertions under mode 3.
